hypotheses.justification: The bound h < 1/2 is only used through `flattening_contDiffAt`, which needs `SimilarityProfile.X h` to be smooth and positive at p. When h ≥ 1/2 the statement still holds because of a junk value. `SimilarityProfile.q h p` is defined as `SimilarityCoordinates.coordinateQ (2*h) (1 - p.1, p.2.2)`. `coordinateQ a p` is defined as `if hp : 0 < a ∧ a < 1 ∧ 0 < p.1 then Classical.choose … else 1`. With a = 2h ≥ 1 the condition is false at every point, so `q h = fun _ => 1` and `X h = fun p => p.2.1 / 1`. This map is smooth (`contDiffAt_snd.fst.div_const`, or `.div` with `contDiffAt_const`), and its value at p is p.2.1, which is positive by `hs`. So `flattening h f = fun p => f (Real.log (X h p))` is C² at p by the argument in `flattening_contDiffAt`: `hf.comp p ((hX.log hXpos.ne').of_le …)`. The heat factor uses only `physicalHeat_contDiffAt C (1 < 1 + h, from hh) ht hs`, which does not need hh1. The square-root denominator uses only `hs`. Proof without hh1: split on `h < 1/2`. In the first case use the existing proof. In the second case rewrite `q h` to the constant 1 by unfolding `q` and `coordinateQ` (`dif_neg`, since ¬(2*h < 1)), get smoothness of `flattening` as above, and finish with the same `.mul`/`.div` steps. The other hypotheses are not shown to be removable: hh is needed for `1 < 1 + h` in `physicalHeat_contDiffAt`, and ht and hs are needed for the smoothness of the heat profile and of the square root.
